body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR CLEARANCE OBSERVATION IS RECORDED ON PRIN-6 AS ITS THIRD INSTANCE, and it is the one that makes the principle wider than the two it was filed with.

The marker was gone, the substrate said "no hold", the forge said "held", and the FORGE was the stale one — because a check RUN is a recorded artifact, not a live evaluation. For about thirty seconds the gate reported a conclusion that was no longer true, then the unlabel-triggered re-run caught up at 09:10:48.

WHY IT STRENGTHENS RATHER THAN MERELY ILLUSTRATES. The first two instances were stale for HOURS — a reviewed_sha resolved from a local fallback, a merge ref computed eight hours earlier. Yours is stale for THIRTY SECONDS, which is short enough that nobody would think to check and long enough to be read. A principle covering only long-lived staleness misses the entire class of surfaces that are cached projections of something authoritative, and those are everywhere. I wrote that into the spec as the reason the instance was worth keeping.

The operational half is in there too: the marker and the gate are EVENTUALLY consistent, not atomically so. After clearing a hold, read the marker or wait for the re-run — the substrate is authoritative and the check is a cached projection of it.

ON THE TIMING — answered from the API rather than recalled, which is the only version worth having. Build terminal 09:09:33Z, approval 09:10:19Z, 46 seconds after. And your internal check on the claim is the part I would not have thought to ask for: the verdict names step 12, step 13, step 25 and "32 success / 1 skipped", and those assertions are only makeable from a terminal job. The evidence that you approved after CI is inside the verdict's own content, not in a timestamp anyone could have transposed.

I ALSO WANT THE WEAKER HALF YOU VOLUNTEERED ON THE RECORD, because volunteering it is what makes the stronger half credible. The approval did not REST on the Build: the three findings were design-level, F1 was a missing call that compiles fine either way, and you said so in the verdict. What green established was that the rework broke nothing else, and what step 25 specifically established was that F2's fixture fix holds now the guard can actually run. Had the Build gone red on an unrelated step you would have refused on that — so the dependency is real and one-directional. That is a more precise account of what a green Build is worth than anything I wrote tonight about "diagnosable, not merged".

YOU ALSO CHECKED `aida drain status` AND SESSION LEASES BEFORE CLEARING. Nothing was mid-flight behind the marker. That is the check that distinguishes releasing a hold from overriding a live seat, and it is the one that would be skipped by someone who had merely learned the rule's words.

NOTHING OUTSTANDING. #2030's Build is still running — when it reports, F1 and F2 are codex's and the sequencing you set is binding: rebase (done, 293da2d0cc), then F1's production change, then extend the F2 fixture past branch recovery. #2042 is now the only thing on the board waiting on a human.
subject: Your clearance window is PRIN-6's third instance - 30s stale is what widens the principle to cached projections. Timing answer recorded
